title: Twisted feline-vibrissa / shrimp-chitin / bacterial-cellulose biotube with human-milk-of-boy-mother branch
central_invariants: INFANT_SEX_IS_NOT_ASSUMED_TO BE A MODERN MATERIALS VARIABLE

textual_correction_gate.prior_overstrong_claim: A prior project summary treated London Medical Papyrus / burn material as a same-mixture CAT_HAIR + MILK_OF_WOMAN_WHO_BORE_A_BOY + RESIN bridge.

verified_split.source: London Medical Papyrus burn spell/remedy cluster

textual_correction_gate.corrected_historical_verdict: CAT_HAIR_AND_BOY_MILK_ARE_BOTH_ATTESTED_IN_EGYPTIAN_BURN_MEDICINE, BUT THE CHECKED PRIMARY TEXTS DO_NOT YET PLACE CAT_HAIR AND BOY_MILK IN THE SAME VERIFIED RECIPE.
textual_correction_gate.supersession_rule: Any registry or prose statement asserting a verified same-recipe CAT_HAIR + BOY_MILK bridge is superseded by this correction unless a primary text is later produced.

modern_materials_branch.human_milk_branch_question: How would a BC-producing SCOBY-derived consortium behave if the liquid phase were human milk from a woman who had borne a male infant, preserving the ancient Egyptian ingredient class as a historical comparison while testing the modern material hypothesis independently?

lactose.prediction: Potential carbon source, but lactose utilization by Komagataeibacter is strain-dependent and generally less favorable than glucose in published BC systems.

human_milk_oligosaccharides.role: complex prebiotic glycans with selective antimicrobial/ecological effects
human_milk_oligosaccharides.prediction: Likely to reshape community ecology more than to behave like freely available glucose for BC synthesis.

proteins.prediction: Protein-rich matrix can change viscosity, interfaces and microbial selection; lactoferrin and lysozyme provide antimicrobial pressure.

lipids.prediction: Milk fat globules may partition to interfaces, coat growing cellulose or reinforcement surfaces, alter oxygen transfer and produce a more heterogeneous BC/protein/lipid composite rather than pure BC.

native_microbiome.fact: Human milk is not sterile and normally contains a microbial community.
native_microbiome.prediction: Adding a SCOBY consortium to untreated human milk creates a mixed-community system with substantially higher ecological uncertainty than a defined BC medium.

literature_anchors.finding: Komagataeibacter rhaeticus MSCL 1463 can use lactose and galactose for BC synthesis, but BC production on whey was about 40-50% lower than on standard glucose medium and lactose assimilation was limited.

Kombucha/SCOBY cultures have been used experimentally to ferment conventional and lactose-free dairy milk, establishing that milk-like matrices can support mixed SCOBY fermentation under controlled food-research conditions.
Human milk contains antimicrobial factors including lactoferrin, lysozyme and sIgA, and human-milk oligosaccharides exert selective antimicrobial and anti-adhesion effects.
Human milk contains its own microbiome and is not sterile.

mechanistic_prediction.overall: BC FORMATION IS PLAUSIBLE IN PRINCIPLE BUT EXPECTED TO BE LESS PREDICTABLE AND POTENTIALLY LOWER-YIELD THAN A STANDARD GLUCOSE BC MEDIUM; COMMUNITY COMPOSITION AND MATERIAL PURITY WOULD BECOME MAJOR VARIABLES.
likely_effects: slower or reduced cellulose output if the dominant BC producer poorly accesses lactose
stronger strain dependence than in glucose/sucrose media
competition or facilitation among SCOBY yeasts, acetic-acid bacteria, native milk microbes and any lactic-acid bacteria present
antimicrobial selection pressure from lactoferrin, lysozyme, sIgA and HMOs
protein/lipid adsorption into or onto the BC matrix
possible opaque, softer or more compositionally heterogeneous material compared with purified BC
oxygen transfer could become even more important in a narrow tube because milk fat/protein films may alter interfaces
the final material cannot be assumed sterile, edible, medical, skin-safe or equivalent to ordinary BC
important_uncertainties: Komagataeibacter strain identity and lactose utilization
whether any observed filament is cellulose rather than mixed biomass/protein precipitate

infant_sex_gate.ancient_textual_fact: Egyptian medical texts repeatedly specify milk of a woman who has borne a son/male child in certain remedies and incantations.
infant_sex_gate.modern_scientific_status: Human studies report limited and sometimes conflicting infant-sex-associated differences in milk composition; a large prospective cohort found no meaningful sex difference in many hormones/cytokines and only a small transient glucose difference.
infant_sex_gate.materials_conclusion: NO ROBUST BASIS EXISTS TO TREAT MALE-INFANT STATUS AS A NECESSARY BC-FORMATION VARIABLE.
infant_sex_gate.interpretive_boundary: For the modern project, BOY_MILK is preserved as an ancient-text historical variable, not promoted to a biochemical requirement.

minimum_non_operational_comparison_logic.preferred_first_step: Use a defined human-milk-analog research medium rather than human milk to isolate lactose/protein/lipid effects before any institutionally governed human-derived-material work.

safety_boundary.human_milk: Human milk is nutrient rich and non-sterile. Although ordinary storage/feeding is not treated as a biohazard, deliberate mixed-microbial culturing changes the risk context. This artifact does not provide a home fermentation protocol for human milk.
safety_boundary.consumption: Do not consume or feed any experimentally fermented human-milk/SCOBY material described by this research branch.
safety_boundary.human_derived_material: Any real human-milk culture experiment belongs under appropriate institutional/laboratory handling, consent, containment and disposal procedures.
safety_boundary.cat_material: Only naturally shed vibrissae are ethically admissible.
safety_boundary.shellfish: Shrimp-derived chitin remains subject to residual protein/allergen characterization and handling controls.
